newsitem.title: FINLAND: Kesko says Tuko ball still in EU's court.
newsitem.headline: Kesko says Tuko ball still in EU's court.

text.p: Finnish wholesale and retail group Kesko Oy said on Wednesday it was waiting for the EU Commission to set the guidelines for how Kesko should eliminate its dominant domestic market position in daily goods.
"We are waiting for the commission's second decision ... on the measures (that could be used) ... to achieve it," Kesko deputy CEO Timo Karake told Finnish radio news in an interview.

The EU Commission earlier ruled that Kesko's purchase in May of domestic rival Tuko Oy was incompatible with the common market because it had given Kesko a dominant domestic market position in daily consumer goods retail and cash & carry.
In a statement, Kesko said the commission had said it "will, in a separate decision ... adopt appropriate measures in order to restore conditions of effective competition."
Karake said these measures would be decisive.
"When we find out what kind of possibilities we receive from the commission ... all depends on that," he said.
The necessary arrangements would in any case be found in the area of daily consumer goods, Karake said.
He said he could not guess when the commission's second decision would come, but that he expected it to be "quite soon".
